summary:
SIDERAKOR AND THE COSMIC RESCUE is an educational, inclusive, and bilingual website designed to teach space science without communication barriers. The project was developed by Team EFATÁ SPACE 47 for the Abandoned but not Forgotten challenge.
• The Problem. New generations are forgetting the valuable historical NASA equipment that remains on the Moon and Mars. Additionally, children with hearing or speech disabilities face serious communication barriers to accessing scientific learning. 
• The Solution. An interactive website created on Google Sites that combines a space adventure story in two languages (Spanish and English) with pop-up educational pages called "Science Classroom." 
• Story and Inclusion. The plot follows the diverse SIDERAKOR team, made up of scientists from five continents and led by Mateo (Peru). In it, characters Leo (USA) and Valentina (Peru) lead a space rescue while communicating through American Sign Language (ASL) and Peruvian Sign Language (LSP).
Expected Impact. To inspire both children and young listeners as well as non-listeners to take an interest in aerospace engineering. It shows that science progresses faster when communication barriers are removed and collaboration is equal.
details:
Objective: to connect and inspire people with space science through a story, demonstrating that removing communication barriers allows brilliant minds to lead the rescue of humanity.

Space Problem: Valuable NASA equipment on the Moon and Mars is forgotten by new generations.

Social Problem: Children with language disabilities face communication barriers to learning science.

Our Mission: To remove these barriers to access to science through this space story.

IMPACT

• Educational Impact: Inspires hearing and non-hearing children and Young people to take an interest in aerospace engineering.

Sources

NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA)

NASA Royal Science and Engineering

1. The Intrepid Lunar Module (LM) (Ascent Stage and Descent Stage)

2. The ALSEP (Apollo 12 Lunar Surface Experiment Package).

3. The Surveyor 3 Probe.

4. The S-Band and VHF Antennas of the Lunar Module.

Tools: Google Sites, Gemini, PowerPoint, Word, PDF.
